newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl to sign German-Czech treaty in Prague.
newsitem.headline: Kohl to sign German-Czech treaty in Prague.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl will travel to Prague on January 21 to take part in the signing of a German-Czech post-World War Two reconciliation accord, government spokesman Peter Haussmann said on Tuesday.
Haussmann said Kohl would be in Prague on January 21 and January 22, but the final details of the trip had not yet been completed.

The Czech Republic and Germany concluded nearly two years of delicate negotiations in December over the text of the joint declaration aimed at ending ill-feeling and suspicion lingering after World War Two and its aftermath.
In the declaration Bonn expresses sorrow over the 1938-45 Nazi occupation of the Czech lands. Prague expresses its regret for Czech brutality in the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans.
The text has been approved by both governments, which have each said it should not be changed by their parliaments.
The Bonn parliament will debate the declaration next week.
